newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares close mixed, focus on leading shares.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares close mixed, focus on leading shares.

text.p: Russian shares closed mixed on Friday as investors focused on leading stocks, which have fallen recently, while less liquid shares fell into hibernation, traders said.
The Russian Trading System of 24 leading shares fell by 0.071 percent to 185.14 on $11.87 million in volume.
"Many investors have long been seeing blue chip prices as at good buy levels," said Maxim Perlin, head of sales and trade at UFG.
Traders said most interest was in UES and LUKoil.
They said UES prices were spurred by the nearing deadline of December 23 for bids in an auction for 8.5 percent of its shares.

"Someone decided to buy, obviously sharing the prevailing point of view that after all the holidays there will be a rise on the market," said Andrei Galperin, a trader from Creditanstalt-Grant. "UES and LUKoil shares are attractive for those who can hold long positions."
UES rose to $0.0850 from $0.0835 at Thursday's close and LUKoil rose to $10.45 from $10.00 after a recent report on their nine-month profits.
"The market is up, but only in some positions," Perlin said. "Its major part is quite slack. It looks like there is a reshuffle in portfolios: some positions are being augmented or reshuffled."
Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at IK Prospekt, said Russian traders bought Purneftegaz and Irkutskenergo, seeing the best growth opportunities in these stocks.
Purneftegaz rose to $2.335 from $2.200 at Wednesday's close, when it was last traded, Irkutskenergo was $0.127 after $0.122 at Thursday's close.
Perlin said regional telecommunication companies, which were the hit of the season in autumn, had become popular again.
"After a fall investors reevaluated their interests and at current level regional shares became attractive again," he said.
Traders forecast a dead market until mid-January.

Komineft fell to $1.25 from $1.6 on December 10, when it was last traded, Norisk Nickel edged down to $5.15 from $5.20 at Thursday's close, Yuganskeneftegaz was $9.70 after $9.85 at Wedensday' close, when it was last traded and Volgotanker rose to $3.25 from $2.90 at Tuesday's close, when it was last traded.
